sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: Nobody pays for FOSS, we can force them to
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
The first time I thought it would be a good idea to write a blog post about the economics of open source was 2013, so this post has been in the works a while. The closest I got before today was 2022, when I wrote a stream-of-consciousness rant into my iOS notes that ended with basically "nothing fucking works". And then that sat there for 4 more years, because "nothing works" is too depressing to bother writing 5000 words about. Now, finally, I have an idea. It's gonna take 5000 words to get there, though, so if you don't have that kind of time, skip to the part about registries.

I've written before about hawks and doves, which is a model from evolutionary biology. You have a population of animals competing for some resource. Some of them fight for it (hawks) and some of them share it (doves). A population that is all hawks is unstable: everybody's constantly getting hurt, and the first two doves to show up cooperate with each other and out-compete everyone. A population that is all doves is unstable too: the first hawk to show up competes with everybody and wins every time. What's stable is a mixture of both types, in proportions such that changing your behaviour doesn't help you, so nobody does. That mix is called an evolutionarily stable strategy, or ESS, and the important word is "stable." It's not the best strategy (arguably that's all doves, where nobody gets hurt), it's just the one the population ends up at and can't leave. I find it a useful way of thinking about software, because software has hawks and doves too.

Closed source is the hawk. It competes: it withholds the code, charges a premium for having something nobody else has, and fights to keep it that way. Open source is the dove. It cooperates: it gives the code away and takes the gains from everybody else giving theirs away too. The resource they're competing over is money, ultimately, though it shows up first as users and as developer attention.

The equilibrium we've landed on is very specific. The evolutionarily stable strategy for a piece of software is "anybody may use this for anything, including commercially, for free." That's MIT, BSD, Apache, the licenses that ask for nothing. Every project that has tried to be a slightly less generous dove has lost to a project that stayed a full dove, and I can give you a lot of examples:

Nobody who has tried to charge for open source at the license level has held the line against a competently run fork, and I don't think that's because of ideology. The people running those companies would love to charge for their code, and most of the people forking it don't care much about freedom in the abstract. It's because of the structure of the market. Disruption, in the original sense, is when a much worse and much cheaper product takes over the bottom of the market, then gets gradually better until it's eaten the whole thing, and there's nothing to stop that process repeating until the product costs nothing at all. Software has been getting disrupted like this for as long as there has been software, and what you end up with is a market with two halves: an enormous cheap half that nearly everybody uses, and a much smaller expensive half that makes nearly all of the money. Android has the market share and iOS has the profits, and they are both gigantic successes depending on which number you're looking at. Free wins share and closed wins profit, and both of them win.

So far this is fine. Free software wins, closed software makes money, everybody has a niche. The problem is what the free layer looks like from the inside.

Sixty percent of open source maintainers are not paid for the work. That's from Tidelift's 2024 survey, and it's the same number they got in 2023, and the same number they got in 2021. Of the unpaid ones, 61% work alone. Nearly 60% of all maintainers have quit or thought about quitting, and the reasons they give are the ones you'd guess: they have a life, they lost interest, they burned out.

The amount of software those people are holding up is silly. Sonatype looked at 1.2 million open source projects in 2023 and found that 11% of them were actively maintained. The Linux Foundation's Census II found that 136 developers wrote more than 80% of the code in the fifty most-used packages. A Harvard study estimated that if open source disappeared, companies would have to spend $8.8 trillion to replace it, and found that 5% of developers produce 96% of that value. This is the JavaScript ecosystem's whole personality, for what it's worth: a huge number of tiny packages with one maintainer, or less than one, sitting at the bottom of the dependency trees of companies that have bet their businesses on them. I spent five years at npm watching this happen and it never stopped being alarming.

The example everybody uses now is xz. In 2024 it turned out that a compression library present in more or less every Linux machine on earth had a backdoor in it, inserted over two years by a fake contributor who had, very patiently, socially engineered the one unpaid person maintaining it into handing over the keys. The maintainer had said publicly that he was struggling and couldn't keep up, and rather than anybody funding him, somebody groomed him. The backdoor was caught by a Microsoft engineer who noticed SSH was taking half a second longer than it should, which is not the kind of defence you want to be relying on.

Now, the popular way to tell this story is "the system is breaking," and I don't think that's right, and the distinction matters. The system isn't breaking. It's stable, at a level of human cost we've collectively decided to put up with. A maintainer burns out, somebody else picks it up, they burn out, and so on. Serial near-burnout isn't a bug in the equilibrium, it is the equilibrium. Open source is very old, and if this was going to collapse it would have done so by now. This is a machine that runs on blood, and because it is the evolutionarily stable strategy, we have been powerless to change it.

But it feels like the problem is getting worse, doesn't it? If a stable system is producing worse outcomes than it used to, one of the inputs moved. The one that moved is speed.

Linux accumulated slowly, so you could maintain a chunk of the kernel on nights and weekends for a decade, because nobody was waiting on you. Then the web happened, and then npm happened, and a million tiny modules appeared in about ten years, any one of which could become load-bearing for somebody's production system within weeks of being published. The software got important faster than any institution could notice it was important, never mind fund it. Meanwhile security got faster too: a bug in a popular library is now exploited within days and lands on tens of thousands of companies at once. So the cost of maintaining a popular package went up a lot, and the payoff for maintaining it stayed exactly where it was, which is zero dollars and a warm feeling.

Nights and weekends stopped being enough, and people kept doing it anyway, because they were always going to write the software. Developers write software the way singers sing, which is to say they'd do it if nobody was listening, and that isn't a problem to be fixed, it's the thing that makes the whole system work. Any proposed solution that involves developers writing less software, or writing less generously, is a non-starter with me. The problem isn't that people write software for free. It's that we've arranged things so the people who write the most useful software for free get a second unpaid job as a reward.

This is the depressing bit, and it's the bit I've been putting off for four years, so let's get through it quickly. Here is what we've tried:

Look at what all of these have in common. They're all voluntary. Companies are asked to give, and some do, and most don't, and the ones that don't get exactly the same software as the ones that do. Charity doesn't scale, and nobody has the authority to issue a mandate. We have been asking companies to pay for open source for thirty years, and I think we can consider asking to be fully tested.

Here's the thing that made me realize I'd been thinking about this wrong: companies already pay for open source, quite a lot of money in fact, they just don't pay it to maintainers.

JFrog sells Artifactory, which is a private mirror that sits between your build servers and the public package registries. JFrog had $532 million in revenue in 2025, up 24%. Snyk, which scans your dependencies for vulnerabilities, is at about $326 million a year. Docker, which runs the registry every container image comes from, is at $207 million. Chainguard, which sells hardened versions of open source images, went from about $40 million to a target of $100 million in a year. Sonatype is private, but it both runs Maven Central, the registry every Java build pulls from, and sells Nexus, the mirror you put in front of it; by Sonatype's own numbers 86% of Maven Central's traffic comes from cloud providers, which is to say from companies. Add Sonar, which now owns Tidelift, and Socket, and the rest of the supply chain security market, and you're comfortably over a billion dollars a year.

What is all that money for? Strip off the marketing and every one of these companies is selling the same thing, which is dependable supply of free code. Your builds don't break when the registry goes down. Your dependencies are cached, scanned, signed, and provably what they say they are. When the next Log4Shell happens you can find out in an hour which of your two thousand services is affected. That's a real product solving a real problem, and companies buy it enthusiastically, because "the free thing we depend on might be broken or malicious and we can't tell" is exactly the kind of problem a procurement department knows how to spend money on.

I want to be clear that I don't think these companies are villains. Several of them are run by people I like. They're solving the actual problem, which is that companies need to be able to depend on code they didn't write and can't inspect. They're just solving it at the wrong layer. They sell insurance against the maintainer, when the maintainer is the one person in the chain who can actually make the code more secure, and she gets nothing while a company two layers up gets paid to tell you whether she did.

This changed my whole view of the problem. For years I assumed the constraint was the supply of money: companies simply would not pay for open source and no mechanism could make them, and Lorenc's story fits that. But the JFrog invoice says otherwise: companies will pay for open source, happily, when it shows up as a boring line item labelled "supply chain." The supply of money was never the problem, the problem is where it gets captured on the way down.

So why doesn't the ESS apply here? If free always wins, why hasn't a free mirror eaten JFrog?

Because there are two games going on, and they have different winners. In the code game the resource is the software itself, and free wins every time, because anybody can copy code, so any attempt to charge for it invites a copy that doesn't. In the supply game the resource is not having to think about where the code comes from, and that game is won by whoever is the default.

Look at the evidence. Nobody has ever successfully forked a registry. Free mirrors of npm, PyPI and Docker Hub exist, are trivial to run, and in some cases are one command away, and companies pay JFrog half a billion dollars a year regardless. Red Hat lost the desktop to Ubuntu, which was funded by a rich guy giving it away, and lost it decisively; the dove won the code game. Red Hat then sold to IBM for $34 billion and makes north of $6 billion a year selling companies supply of the same free code with a phone number attached. Anybody could have had the same code for free, and lots of them did, but a very large number of companies paid Red Hat anyway.

Docker is the clearest example because it happened recently and in public. In November 2020 Docker Hub started rate-limiting anonymous and free pulls. In August 2021 Docker Desktop became a paid product for any company with more than 250 employees or $10 million in revenue, and stayed free for individuals, small companies and open source projects. If free always won, a free alternative should have eaten them, and Podman and containerd exist and are free and are perfectly fine. Instead Docker's revenue went from roughly $12 million in 2020 to over $50 million in 2021 to $207 million in 2024, with more than a million paid seats. (Docker also tried announcing per-pull consumption charges and then cancelled them in 2025 after developers rioted, which tells you exactly what shape of charge works: bill the company, not the download. Nobody wants a bill that goes up every time CI reruns.)

Free wins the code game, but the supply game is won by whoever is the default, and defaults can charge. The registries are the one place in the whole system where the two games touch, because they are where free code turns into supply, and unlike a license, a registry can't be routed around by copying, because it's not a legal restriction, it's an extremely convenient piece of infrastructure. They don't want to route around it; routing around it is a pain in the ass worth paying to avoid.

At this point somebody is going to say "hasn't this been tried?", and the answer is sort of, and the ways it failed are instructive. I'm going to define "the registry layer" narrowly: whoever owns the domain that everybody is downloading stuff from. By that definition almost nothing on this list counts.

In August 2019 Feross Aboukhadijeh, who maintained a hundred-odd npm packages including Standard, started printing sponsor messages in the terminal during npm install. Developers hated it, the sponsors backed out within days, and Feross wrote it up as a failed experiment. npm's response was to ban terminal ads in its terms of service and ship npm fund, which prints a list of donation links. That's the one time the actual registry has intervened in funding, and what it did was take away a way of getting money and replace it with a hyperlink. That is some weak tea. In my time at npm we never had the courage to try anything more extreme, and we should have.

Flossbank, from 2020 to 2022, wrapped npm and yarn, collected small donations or ad revenue, and split it across the whole dependency tree of whatever you installed. That is the payout half of what I'm about to propose, built and working. It shut down, and the founder's post-mortem is honest about why: it was opt-in, and opt-in dies of "why should I pay if the next guy doesn't." Flossbank also wasn't the registry, it was a thing you installed in front of the registry, which is enough friction that nobody bothers.

Ruby Together, from 2015 to 2022, collected membership fees from companies to fund work on RubyGems and Bundler. It worked, modestly, until it merged into Ruby Central, whose dependence on one big sponsor then produced the 2025 takeover of the RubyGems repositories, a bunch of resignations, and a depleted team facing the worst attack on a registry in years the following spring. That was funding for the registry's own operations, not for the packages in it, and it was voluntary, and it had one big donor, which is three separate ways to fail.

So the pattern is: everything voluntary died of free riding, and the one thing that wasn't voluntary (Docker) worked and kept the money for itself. Nobody who owns the domain has ever charged companies for supply and paid the people who make the supply worth having.

So here's the proposal. There are three parts, none of them new; what's new is putting them in the same place.

First, the registries meter corporate use and charge for it. They already meter it. npm, PyPI, Docker Hub and Maven Central all have rate limits, authentication and enterprise tiers, and the mirror vendors that sit in front of them bill by the seat. Docker's rule is the right rule: individuals, small teams, students and open source projects pay nothing and notice nothing. A company above some size gets a subscription, priced the way a JFrog or Docker subscription is priced today, which is to say at a level procurement signs without scheduling a meeting. For most of these companies it isn't even a new cost, because they're already paying it; the invoice just gets a new line.

Second, a fixed slice of that revenue is a royalty, and it goes to the packages. Not to the registry, not to a foundation, not to a grants committee with an application form. Pro rata, to every package that shows up in the paying customer's dependency trees, weighted by how many paying customers depend on it, automatically, every month, with no ceremony and no thank-you email, because the whole point is that nobody has to do anything for the money to move. My 2022 notes have a line about this that I'll leave unedited: "The money has to go in one end and out the other. You don't have to use crypto to do this, that would be bad, just use a database." The payout half is not hard. thanks.dev does pro rata distribution over dependency trees today, and Flossbank did it in 2020. Nobody's ever connected it to the collection half.

Third, the people who do this are the people who own the domains. There are about a dozen registries that matter. Every maintainer already has an account on the one they care about, with a name attached and a way to get paid either present or one form field away. The billing side is finite: a few thousand large companies, most of whom are already customers of somebody in the supply chain. The two hardest problems in every previous attempt, finding the payers and finding the payees, are already solved, and they're solved by the same database.

disagreements: 开源危机本质：传统叙事认为是‘开源系统正在走向崩溃’，而作者认为这是一种‘以人类无偿劳动甚至心理损耗为代价但演化稳定的残酷均衡（ESS）’
资金短缺的归因：通常观点认为‘企业不愿为开源出资’，作者则指出‘企业实际上愿意且已经在供应链安全中介层支付了数十亿美元，只是资金流向了错误的层级’
治理手段的有效性：行业普遍依赖企业CSR捐款、开源基金会支持或宽松许可证道德约束，而作者暗示自愿性路线已经失败，倾向于探索包仓库/注册表（registries）层面的强制性收费机制

忽略了企业直接雇佣开源核心开发者全职维护项目的既有模式，及其为何无法覆盖长尾关键模块的深层组织矛盾
将供应链安全工具简单归纳为‘针对维护者的保险’，可能低估了构建自动化构建管线、合规性审计、漏洞快速定位等中介产品本身的工程复杂度和真实价值

sourceOnlyStories.fullContent: The International Energy Agency expects coal demand to increase this year in response to ongoing oil and gas trade constraints stemming from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Several countries have been forced to turn back to coal to fill the gap, as oil inventories are depleted and countries gradually expand their renewable energy capacity. In its mid-year update, the IEA predicted that coal use would likely increase in some regions of the world owing to higher natural gas prices in 2026. The conflict in the Middle East and ongoing restrictions on trade via the Strait of Hormuz maritime trade corridor have driven up prices in recent months. This has led to severe global energy disruptions, pushing oil and gas prices higher. The massive reduction in LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has led some countries to face energy shortages, requiring them to turn to other energy sources. Japan, India, Bangladesh, the Philippines, South Korea, Thailand, Taiwan, China, and some European countries have been forced to increase their coal use to fill the gap. In addition, some countries are not only turning to coal for power; China's coal consumption for chemical product production has also increased in recent months due to high oil prices. Coal consumption may increase further in some regions of the world in the coming months if a particularly strong El Nio weather pattern occurs, as predicted. Higher-than-normal temperatures and lower hydropower output could drive up power demand across Asia, in large markets such as India and Vietnam. Global coal production matched a record high in 2025 but is expected to decrease slightly year over year in 2026. Despite that, the IEA expects demand for the energy commodity to rise by 1.2 per cent in 2026, bringing the world's consumption to a record 8.94 billion metric tonnes. Coal demand by the world's two biggest coal consumers, China and India, is expected to rise by 1 per cent and 4.2 per cent respectively, to 5 billion tonnes and 1.353 billion tonnes. The outlook for 2027 is murkier given the unpredictability of trade in the Strait of Hormuz. If LNG flows recover next year, it could drive natural gas prices down, spurring a shift in gas and coal use. However, global demand will likely increase if energy trade remains restricted. "Although shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz do not directly affect coal markets" and virtually no coal shipments pass through the Strait of Hormuz, "tighter natural gas supply has pushed up prices, prompting some electricity systems to switch from gas to coal," the IEA stated. News of increased coal use is concerning, given that the United Nations UN has, for the first time, acknowledged that the world is set to overshoot its target of limiting global warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels. As part of efforts to support a global green transition and uphold climate pledges, diplomats from almost every country agreed to "phase down" global coal consumption at the 2021 COP26 climate summit in Glasgow. However, since the signing of the agreement, several countries have continued to rely on coal burning to meet rising electricity demand. While many countries are investing heavily in accelerating the development of their renewable energy sectors, it is expected to take several years to eliminate the need for fossil fuels for power in most countries. In March, Italy announced plans to postpone the shutdown of its coal-fired power plants for all of 13 years. Germany has also announced it is considering restarting some of its coal plants to meet the country's energy demand. In March, Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated, "We must supply this country with electricity. I am not prepared to jeopardise the core of our industry simply because we have adopted phase-out plans that have become unrealistic." Somewhat surprisingly, given President Trump's aim to revive the ageing coal sector, coal consumption in the United States is expected to fall by around 7 per cent this year, following an unexpected jump last year. The United States has been largely sheltered from the global gas disruption thanks to its abundant, cheap domestic natural gas. Vast quantities of U.S. solar and wind energy have also come online this year, following years of accelerated development, further reducing the need for coal. Nevertheless, the United States made a significant contribution to the increase in global emissions in 2025. According to the Energy Institute, global energy-related carbon dioxide emissions rose by 1.1 per cent to 35.806 billion tonnes, with the United States accounting for about 13.3 per cent of the increase in direct energy-related CO2 emissions. Under a broader measure that also includes methane and flaring emissions, the United States accounted for roughly a third of the global increase. This demonstrates just how detrimental an increase in coal consumption can be for global emissions, with coal-related emissions expected to climb significantly this year in line with higher consumption. By Felicity Bradstock for Oilprice.com

Dan Tehan , the shadow minister for energy, said Gallagher’s criticism of the Coalition’s fuel plan wasn’t fair.

Tehan said the call for a 50% cut to the fuel excise whenever barrels of oil top US$100 was a “good, sensible, practical measure” that would help Australians deal with a cost of living crisis. He told RN:

[What] I would say to Anthony Albanese and the Labor party is get out amongst the people and see what’s happening in your electorates because people are hurting because of cost of living …

We have the discipline to be able to do the policy work to make sure we can offset policies like this so it won’t be inflationary and it will provide much needed relief to people, and they need it now.

Obviously we’ve helped when the war started with some changes to the fuel excise but we’ve shifted, and [are] including in the budget, to providing more permanent cost of living arrangements, including through the tax system, to make sure that that ongoing cost-of-living help is there permanently, not just in these one-off arrangements, which, when we’ve got higher inflation, could be difficult in the economy.

Our decisions have been built and baked into the budget to make sure that that cost-of-living help is permanent. You know, the sooner this war in the Middle East stops, the better.

worldStories.originalTitle: Jets collapse late against Packers, miss chance at first 2-0 start since 2015 in overtime loss
worldStories.snippet: The New York Jets blew a 17-7 fourth quarter lead as the Green Bay Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime at MetLife Stadium.
worldStories.fullContent:
For most of Sunday afternoon, the New York Jets looked poised to move to 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Jets controlled most of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, but made some crucial errors down the stretch to cough up their 10-point fourth-quarter lead.

The Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime, with Trey Smack kicking a 26-yard field goal to complete the comeback.

Green Bay struck first on a 6-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to MarShawn Lloyd in the second quarter, but the Jets answered with a 5-yard touchdown run from Braelon Allen. Geno Smith connected with Garrett Wilson for a 5-yard score in the third quarter to give New York a 14-7 lead.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Jets appeared to have delivered the knockout blow early in the fourth quarter when they recovered a Lloyd fumble at the Green Bay 18-yard line. But the offense couldn't move the ball and settled for a 32-yard Jason Sanders field goal, extending the lead to 17-7 with 11:04 remaining.

That's when everything started to unravel.

A 38-yard pass-interference penalty helped Green Bay march down the field before Love found Christian Watson for a 3-yard touchdown. The Jets failed to pick up a first down on their next possession, and Skyy Moore returned the ensuing punt 63 yards to the New York 19-yard line. Smack kicked a 34-yard field goal four plays later to tie the game.

New York still had a chance to win in regulation. After Breece Hall gained just one yard on third-and-2, the Jets faced fourth-and-1 at midfield with 1:20 remaining. Aaron Glenn kept his offense on the field rather than punting, an aggressive decision to try to win the game. It's hard to fault Glenn for trusting his offense to gain one yard, but Braelon Allen was stuffed. Green Bay failed to capitalize, sending the game to overtime.

The Jets received the ball first in overtime and the possession was a complete disaster. The Packers sacked Smith on consecutive plays, the offense committed a false-start penalty and New York faced a third-and-30 from their own 10-yard line before eventually punting on fourth down.

Green Bay then moved 58 yards on four offensive plays, aided by an unnecessary roughness penalty against Jarvis Brownlee Jr., before Smack ended the game on the fifth play of the drive.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Penalties were a problem for both teams throughout the game. Green Bay was flagged 14 times for 133 yards, while New York committed 13 penalties for 156 yards. That's an absurd 27 accepted penalties for 289 yards.

But the timing of the Jets' two biggest penalties proved especially costly: the 38-yard pass-interference call aided Green Bay's fourth-quarter touchdown drive, while Brownlee's 15-yard penalty moved the Packers into position for the winning field goal.

Smith completed 27-of-41 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. It wasn't a spectacular performance, but it should have been good enough given how well New York's defense played.

That's what makes the loss particularly brutal for the Jets. New York outgained Green Bay 285-199, held the Packers to 1-of-9 on third down, won the turnover battle and possessed the ball for nearly 11 minutes longer. Love threw for just 145 yards, although he threw two touchdowns and avoided turning the ball over.

The Jets had the game won and a chance to send the MetLife Stadium crowd home believing in a 2-0 team . Instead, they gave the game away and sent their fans home wondering how they managed to blow another one.
worldStories.fullTranslation:
在周日下午的大部分时间里，纽约喷气机队看起来都胜券在握，有望迎来2015年以来的首次2胜0负开局。在大都会人寿体育场对阵绿湾包装工队的比赛中，喷气机队掌控了大部分时间的局势，但在最后关头犯下了几次致命错误，白白葬送了第四节10分的领先优势。

包装工队连得13分，在加时赛中以20-17获胜，特雷·斯马克（Trey Smack）命中一记26码的射门，完成了这场逆转。

绿湾队在第二节率先发难，乔丹·洛夫（Jordan Love）助攻马肖恩·劳埃德（MarShawn Lloyd）完成6码达阵传球，但喷气机队随后凭借布雷隆·艾伦（Braelon Allen）的5码达阵冲跑还以颜色。第三节，吉诺·史密斯（Geno Smith）与加勒特·威尔逊（Garrett Wilson）连线完成5码达阵得分，让纽约队以14-7取得领先。

点击此处获取更多OUTKICK体育报道

第四节初，喷气机队在绿湾队18码线上抢回了劳埃德的掉球，看似已经给予对手致命一击。但随后进攻端停滞不前，只能由杰森·桑德斯（Jason Sanders）命中一记32码射门，在比赛还剩11分04秒时将领先优势扩大到17-7。

正是从那一刻起，局势开始全面崩盘。

一次38码的传球干扰犯规帮助绿湾队大步推进，随后洛夫连线克里斯蒂安·沃森（Christian Watson）完成3码达阵。喷气机队在接下来的进攻轮次中未能取得首攻，天魔·摩尔（Skyy Moore）将随后的弃踢回攻63码，推进至纽约队19码线。四档进攻后，斯马克命中一记34码射门，将比分扳平。

纽约队在常规时间仍有获胜机会。在布里斯·霍尔（Breece Hall）于三档2码仅推进1码后，喷气机队在比赛还剩1分20秒时面临中场附近的四档1码。主教练阿隆·格伦（Aaron Glenn）没有选择弃踢，而是让进攻组留在场上，做出了一个试图直接拿下比赛的激进决定。很难指责格伦信任自己的进攻组去争取这短短1码，但布雷隆·艾伦的冲球被防守组死死阻截。绿湾队随后未能在常规时间转化为得分，比赛进入加时赛。

喷气机队在加时赛中率先获得球权，但这次进攻堪称一场彻底的灾难。包装工队连续两次抄截史密斯，进攻组又出现一次提前移动犯规，导致纽约队在本方10码线面临三档30码的绝境，最终只能在四档弃踢。

随后，在贾维斯·布朗利二世（Jarvis Brownlee Jr.）被判非必要粗暴犯规的帮助下，绿湾队仅用四次进攻就推进了58码，接着斯马克在这次进攻序列的第五档完成终结绝杀。

克雷格·卡顿秀——直率、犀利、不容错过。立即下载他的每日播客！

犯规整场比赛都困扰着双方。绿湾队被罚14次、罚退133码，而纽约队则出现13次犯规、罚退156码。两队被判罚并接受的犯规累计达到了惊人的27次，总计罚退289码。

然而，喷气机队两次代价最为惨重的犯规发生时机极其致命：那次38码的传球干扰犯规直接助推了绿湾队第四节的达阵推进，而布朗利的15码粗暴犯规更是直接将包装工队送入了绝杀射门的有效射程。

史密斯全场41投27中，推进247码，收获1次达阵，无抄截。这算不上极其惊艳的发挥，但考虑到纽约队防守组的出色表现，这样的数据本应足以赢下比赛。

这正是这场失利让喷气机队尤为痛心疾首的原因所在。纽约队在总推进码数上以285-199领先绿湾队，将包装工队的三档转换限制为9投仅1中，在失误比上占优，且控球时间足足多了近11分钟。洛夫全场仅传出145码，不过他送出了两次达阵并且没有失误送球。

喷气机队本已胜券在握，本有机会让大都会人寿体育场的球迷坚信这是一支能取得2胜0负的队伍并满意而归。然而，他们亲手将胜利拱手相让，让球迷在退场时只能再次陷入沉思：他们究竟是怎么又搞砸了一场比赛？

worldStories.title: 爱国者获胜后弗拉贝尔因德雷克·梅耶状态挣扎怒斥记者：“你休想毁了我的周日”
worldStories.originalTitle: Mike Vrabel snaps at reporter over Drake Maye's struggles after Pats win: 'you're not going to ruin my Sunday'
worldStories.snippet: Mike Vrabel told reporters they wouldn't ruin his Sunday after the Patriots beat the Steelers 20-3, but Drake Maye's struggles still loom large.
worldStories.fullContent:
The New England Patriots got their first win of the season Sunday, and head coach Mike Vrabel wasn't about to let a few perfectly valid questions about his quarterback spoil the celebration.

After New England defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3, Vrabel had a tense exchange with Boston Globe reporter Ben Volin, who pressed him about his level of concern over Drake Maye's performance through the first two weeks of the season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Vrabel wasn't interested in entertaining the question.

"You're not going to ruin my Sunday," the coach fired back.

The exchange continued when reporter Greg Bedard also questioned Vrabel about Maye's struggles, prompting the coach to make it clear that he wasn't going to dwell on the negatives after a victory.

To be fair, though, the reporters had a legitimate reason to ask.

Maye hasn't exactly looked like the quarterback who led New England to the Super Bowl last season, and Sunday's win over Pittsburgh did little to put those concerns to rest.

The 23-year-old completed 14 of 22 passes for 208 yards, no touchdowns and one interception against the Steelers. While he connected with receiver Romeo Doubs for a 63-yard gain, the Patriots struggled to consistently move the ball and finished with just 13 offensive points.

Instead, New England's defense did most of the heavy lifting, holding Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers to just 3 points and 235 total yards.

Rookie running back TreVeyon Henderson provided the Patriots' only offensive touchdown with a 39-yard run in the first quarter. Later, Christian Barmore strip-sacked Rodgers, and Elijah Ponder returned the fumble 19 yards for a touchdown to put the game away.

In other words, the Patriots won comfortably, but Maye wasn't exactly the reason why.

Sunday's performance came just 11 days after a disastrous season opener against the Seattle Seahawks.

In a rematch of Super Bowl LX, Maye threw three fourth-quarter interceptions as New England blew a 10-point lead and lost 13-10. His final interception came in the end zone with just 26 seconds remaining, ending a potential game-tying drive.

Maye finished that game with 178 passing yards, one touchdown and three interceptions. Afterward, he acknowledged that he had abandoned the patient approach that had worked earlier in the game.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"We had the game under control," Maye said following the loss. "Thought we had a good plan to start chipping away and be patient and lost patience, and it cost us, decisions that cost us the game on my part, on my end."

Through two games, Maye has thrown four interceptions and just one touchdown pass.

That's a far cry from his 2025 campaign, when he threw for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns while finishing as the runner-up in NFL MVP voting.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Vrabel is certainly entitled to enjoy Sunday's victory, especially after the Patriots' ugly collapse against Seattle.

Sure, the season is young. No need to overreact.

But with New England's franchise quarterback — so far — struggling to recapture last year's form, the questions about his performance aren't going away simply because Vrabel wants them to.

新英格兰爱国者队在周日收获了本赛季的首场胜利，而主教练迈克·弗拉贝尔（Mike Vrabel）可不打算让几个针对其四分卫的完全合情合理的问题破坏庆祝气氛。

在爱国者队以20-3击败匹兹堡钢人队后，弗拉贝尔与《波士顿环球报》记者本·沃林（Ben Volin）发生了一番剑拔弩张的言语交锋。后者向他施压，追问他对德雷克·梅耶（Drake Maye）在赛季前两周表现的担忧程度。

点击此处获取更多OUTKICK体育报道

弗拉贝尔对回答这个问题毫无兴趣。

“你休想毁了我的周日，”这位教练反唇相讥。

当记者格雷格·贝达德（Greg Bedard）同样质疑弗拉贝尔关于梅耶的挣扎表现时，交锋仍在继续，这促使主教练明确表示，他不会在球队赢球后沉溺于负面问题中。

不过平心而论，记者们提出这些问题有着充分的理由。

梅耶现在的表现可一点都不像上赛季带领新英格兰队杀入超级碗的那名四分卫，而周日对阵匹兹堡的这场胜利也未能平息那些担忧。

这位23岁的四分卫在对阵钢人队的比赛中22投14中，传出208码，没有达阵，并有1次被抄截。尽管他与外接手罗密欧·杜布斯（Romeo Doubs）连线完成了一次63码的长传推进，但爱国者队进攻端难以持续推进，最终进攻组仅拿下13分。

相反，新英格兰队的防守组承担了绝大部分重任，将阿隆·罗杰斯（Aaron Rodgers）和钢人队限制在仅得3分、总码数仅235码的表现。

新秀跑卫特雷维昂·亨德森（TreVeyon Henderson）在第一节完成了一记39码的冲球得分，贡献了爱国者队唯一的进攻达阵。随后，克里斯蒂安·巴莫尔（Christian Barmore）对罗杰斯完成擒杀并造成掉球，伊莱贾·庞德（Elijah Ponder）拾起球回攻19码达阵，彻底终结了比赛悬念。

换句话说，爱国者队轻松赢下了比赛，但梅耶可谈不上是主要功臣。

周日的这一表现，距离他在对阵西雅图海鹰队的灾难性揭幕战仅仅过去了11天。

在那场第60届超级碗的重赛中，梅耶在第四节送出了三次被抄截，导致新英格兰队在手握10分领先优势的情况下被逆转，以10-13失利。他在比赛仅剩26秒时在端区内送出最后一次被抄截，扼杀了可能扳平比分的进攻推进。

梅耶在那场比赛中取得178码传球码数、1次达阵和3次被抄截。赛后他坦承，自己放弃了比赛早段行之有效的耐心战术。

克雷格·卡顿秀——直言不讳、毫不妥协、不容错过。立即下载他的每日播客！

“我们当时掌控了比赛局势，”梅耶在那场失利后表示，“我以为我们制定了很好的计划，一步步推进并保持耐心，但我失去了耐心，这让我们付出了代价，这是我这边的决定导致我们输掉了比赛。”

两场比赛下来，梅耶已经送出4次被抄截，仅传出1次达阵。

这与他在2025赛季的惊艳表现相去甚远——当时他传球推进4394码并拿下31次达阵，在NFL最有价值球员（MVP）评选中名列第二。

弗拉贝尔当然有权享受周日的胜利，尤其是在爱国者队经历对阵西雅图的惨痛崩盘之后。

诚然，赛季才刚刚开始，无需过度反应。

然而，鉴于新英格兰队的这名当家四分卫截至目前仍在苦苦寻找去年的巅峰状态，关于他表现的种种质疑，绝不会仅仅因为弗拉贝尔的主观意愿就此烟消云散。

financeStories.fullContent: In 2024, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a law requiring large fossil fuel polluters to pay up to $75 billion in damages. However, after two years, a federal judge has ruled that the law conflicts with federal law and cannot proceed. The law that Hochul signed in December 2024 would have required companies that contribute heavily to fossil fuel pollution to pay to repair damage caused by extreme weather events, which have become increasingly common as global warming intensifies. The law focuses on pollution produced by the combustion of fossil fuels. A study published in 2025 in the journal Nature linked more than 200 severe heat waves directly to carbon pollution from the world's largest fossil fuel producers. The legislation, known as the Climate Change Superfund Act, mandated that firms responsible for most of the accumulation of carbon emissions between 2000 and 2024 would pay around $3 billion a year for 25 years. The legislation was based on the original Superfund law, established in 1980, which requires companies to pay for toxic waste cleanup activities following incidents such as oil and chemical spills. Upon signing the law, Hochul stated, "With nearly every record rainfall, heat wave, and coastal storm, New Yorkers are increasingly burdened with billions of dollars in health, safety, and environmental consequences due to polluters that have historically harmed our environment." The aim of the law was to reduce the burden on taxpayers by addressing the challenges that big corporations, particularly oil and gas companies, have played a major role in creating, with these companies producing over 1 billion tons of greenhouse gas emissions globally over the 24-year period. The funds would contribute to restoring and protecting coastal wetlands; upgrading roads and bridges; improving stormwater drainage systems; elevating and retrofitting structures; and investing in recovery efforts from natural disasters. However, last month, a federal judge ruled that the New York law conflicted with federal law and therefore could not take effect. The chief judge of the US District Court for the Northern District of New York, Brenda Sannes, ruled that the state could not enforce its "climate superfund" law in a 63-page decision deeming the law "unusual and sweeping". Sannes cited the Second Circuit's 2021 decision in City of New York v. Chevron, a case in which New York sued oil companies seeking climate-change damages, as precedent. Cassidy DiPaola, communications director for organisation Make Polluters Pay, stressed, "This decision rests on contested precedent from a fundamentally different case, and Attorney General Tish James must appeal immediately." Meanwhile, State Senator Liz Krueger, a sponsor of the law, said the ruling was "unfortunate" and emphasised that Judge Sannes had not recognised a distinction between a claim like New York City's and "a state legislature exercising its constitutional powers to raise revenues and protect its citizens." Krueger added that she had expected "many rounds of legal wrangling" before the law could take effect. However, several Republican states and business organisations have criticised the "climate superfund" law over the last two years, arguing that people benefited from the use of fossil fuels during the period in question, during which time renewable alternatives were not readily available. The U.S. Justice Department also argued in support of the lawsuit against the New York law last month, filing its own litigation against it in the Southern District of New York; a suit that is still pending. JB McCuskey, the attorney general of West Virginia, whose office led the challenge against the New York law, stated, "This is a major victory in the fight against liberal states, trying to balance their budgets on the backs of our hard-working men and women in the coal, oil and gas industries." Hochul has not yet said whether New York state plans to appeal the decision. However, Ken Lovett, the senior communications adviser on energy and environment for Governor Hochul, said, "Taxpayers shouldn't have to foot the bill for damages caused by polluters." Lovett added, "We are reviewing the decision to determine possible next steps." Vermont is the only other state to have passed a climate superfund law, and it is now facing a similar lawsuit. While some other states have explored the introduction of a similar fund, no other state has yet announced a formal payment scheme against major emitters. The New York law was originally proposed following years of still-unresolved litigation by state and local governments against fossil fuel companies seeking damages. Many of the suits argue that the firms covered up what they knew about the dangers of global warming for decades. The New York "Superfund" Law will not take effect any time soon, given the recent ruling, and it remains uncertain whether the state government will appeal the decision. Meanwhile, the results of the ongoing legal challenge to a similar law in Vermont could determine whether other states introduce similar legislation. By Felicity Bradstock for Oilprice.com
financeStories.fullTranslation:
2024年，纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔（Kathy Hochul）签署了一项法律，要求大型化石燃料污染企业支付高达750亿美元的赔偿金。然而两年后，一名联邦法官裁定该法律与联邦法律相抵触，无法继续推进。

霍楚尔于2024年12月签署的这项法律本应要求那些对化石燃料污染负有重大责任的公司出资修复因极端天气事件造成的损害，而随着全球变暖的加剧，这类极端天气正变得越来越普遍。该法律聚焦于化石燃料燃烧所产生的污染。2025年发表在《自然》（Nature）杂志上的一项研究，将200多起严重热浪直接与全球最大化石燃料生产商产生的碳污染联系在一起。

这项名为《气候变化超级基金法》（Climate Change Superfund Act）的立法规定，在2000年至2024年间对大部分碳排放积累负有责任的企业，需在25年内每年支付约30亿美元。该法案以1980年确立的最初《超级基金法》（Superfund law）为蓝本，后者要求企业在发生漏油和化学品泄漏等事件后为有毒废弃物的清理行动买单。

在签署该法案时，霍楚尔表示：“几乎每一次打破纪录的暴雨、热浪和沿海风暴，都让纽约人承受着数十亿美元的健康、安全和环境代价，这正是源于那些历史上破坏过我们环境的排污者。”该法律的宗旨是通过应对大企业（尤其是石油和天然气公司）所造成的主要挑战来减轻纳税人的负担；在过去的24年间，这些公司在全球范围内产生了超过10亿吨的温室气体排放。这些资金将用于修复和保护沿海湿地、升级道路与桥梁、改善雨水排放系统、加固和改造建筑物，以及投资于自然灾害后的重建恢复工作。

然而，上个月一名联邦法官裁定，纽约州的这项法律与联邦法律发生冲突，因此无法生效。美国纽约北区联邦地区法院首席法官布伦达·桑内斯（Brenda Sannes）在一份长达63页的判决书中裁定，该州不得执行其“气候超级基金”法，并认为该法“不同寻常且涵盖面过于宽泛”。桑内斯引用了联邦第二巡回上诉法院在2021年“纽约市诉雪佛龙案”（City of New York v. Chevron）中的判决作为先例，当时纽约市起诉石油公司索要气候变化赔偿。

倡导组织“让排污者买单”（Make Polluters Pay）的联络主任卡西迪·迪保拉（Cassidy DiPaola）强调：“这项裁决依赖于一个性质根本不同的案件中所形成的具有争议的先例，司法部长蒂什·詹姆斯（Tish James）必须立即提起上诉。”

与此同时，该法案的发起人、州参议员莉兹·克鲁格（Liz Krueger）表示该裁决“令人遗憾”，并强调桑内斯法官没有将纽约市提出的此类索赔与“州立法机构行使其宪法权力以增加财政收入并保护其公民”区分开来。克鲁格补充称，她早料到在法律生效之前会经历“多轮法律博弈”。

然而，在过去的两年里，一些共和党执政的州和商业组织对这部“气候超级基金”法提出了批评，认为公众在相关时期内从使用化石燃料中获益，且当时尚无容易获取的可再生替代能源。美国司法部上个月也对针对纽约州该法的诉讼表示支持，并在纽约南区联邦地区法院提起了自己的诉讼；该诉讼目前仍在审理中。

牵头对纽约州法律发起挑战的西弗吉尼亚州总检察长JB·麦卡斯基（JB McCuskey）表示：“这是反对自由派州斗争的一次重大胜利，那些州试图把预算平衡建立在我们煤炭、石油和天然气行业勤劳奉献的劳动者背上。”

霍楚尔尚未说明纽约州是否计划对该判决提起上诉。不过，霍楚尔州长负责能源与环境事务的高级传播顾问肯·洛夫特（Ken Lovett）表示：“纳税人不应该为排污者造成的损害买单。”洛夫特补充道：“我们正在审查这项裁决，以确定可能的后续措施。”

佛蒙特州是除纽约州外唯一一个通过了气候超级基金法的州，目前该州也面临着类似的诉讼。虽然其他一些州也在探讨设立类似基金，但尚无其他州宣布针对大型排放企业出台正式的收费方案。纽约州的法律最初是在州和地方政府多年来针对化石燃料公司索赔且悬而未决的诉讼背景下提出的。其中许多诉讼主张，这些企业几十年来一直在隐瞒它们所掌握的全球变暖危险的信息。

鉴于近期的裁决，纽约州的“超级基金”法短期内不会生效，且州政府是否会对该判决提起上诉仍不确定。与此同时，佛蒙特州类似法律所面临的法律挑战的最终结果，可能会决定其他州未来是否会出台类似的立法。

financeStories.title: “太糟糕了”：关税、飙升的燃料成本和走高的利率如何挤压美国企业
financeStories.originalTitle: ‘It's awful’: How tariffs, soaring fuel costs and higher interest rates are squeezing American companies
financeStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
financeStories.source: CNBC Markets (CNBC 市场官方英文)
financeStories.snippet: Tariffs, fuel prices and interest rates are squeezing American companies, particularly manufacturers, auto suppliers, retailers and transportation businesses.
financeStories.fullContent:
Fewer, pricier flights. Freight surcharges. Manufacturers hoarding inventory. Even bankruptcy.

For American companies large and small, the combination of tariffs imposed under President Donald Trump's trade policies, surging fuel prices from the Iran war and, now, rising interest rates is forcing executives to make tough choices.

Allen Eden has been holding onto extra inventory for his 25-person business, the Original Saw Co. in Britt, Iowa, which makes industrial power saws for wood and metalwork, as he grapples with spiking prices for aluminum, steel and essential parts.

One example: A "little bracket" used for his saw motors more than doubled in price this summer, surging to $87 from $42, he said.

"It's awful," Eden, 56, told CNBC. "[I'm] just trying to keep more of the stuff around because I don't know if we can get it down the road."

It's a three-way squeeze for businesses across manufacturing, transportation and retail: Tariffs are making raw materials and goods more expensive. Higher fuel prices are pushing up the cost of making and moving them. And rising rates are making it more expensive to finance the inventory and equipment businesses need to keep running.

While few sectors are completely insulated from these pressures, middle-market manufacturers are caught in a particularly tight vise. Rising steel and fuel costs are forcing them to pass at least some of those expenses on through higher prices, helping feed the stubborn inflation of the past few years.

But to wrangle inflation, the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years and signaled another hike is possible this year. That makes it more expensive for businesses to finance inventory and borrow for growth at the same time that higher input costs and record prices for diesel, which is used for trucking, squeeze margins.

Price increases for Eden's saws, sold both to megaretailers like Home Depot and directly to small- and medium-sized manufacturers, look inevitable, the business owner said.

The pain isn't being evenly distributed. Smaller companies typically rely on shorter-term lending, meaning Fed hikes pass more directly into their costs, JPMorgan Chase global strategy head Dubravko Lakos-Bujas said in a Sept. 14 note.

But regardless of size, capital-intensive sectors like manufacturing and equipment suppliers, logistics firms including trucking fleets, and commercial real estate also suffer more in a rising-rate environment, according to Lakos-Bujas.

"The combination of higher rates and higher fuel prices means that sectors with heavy exposure to both are first in the line of fire," said Gregory Daco, chief economist at EY-Parthenon, the global consulting arm of Ernst & Young.

"Any type of manufacturing is going to be disproportionately exposed to higher fuel prices," he said.

Rising fuel and commodity costs have strained both material makers and the retailers they serve.

Mark Costa, CEO of industrial giant Eastman Chemical, said in May that the one-two punch of interest rates and inflation was forcing his industry into a corner. Eastman makes the plastics, additives, and other materials used in products as diverse as medical devices, animal feed, and car windshields.

"Everyone had their back against the wall and had no room to absorb these increases," Costa said. "Everyone is very quickly raising prices faster than I've ever seen in 20 years."

On the retail side, unexpected pressure from energy and raw materials costs will "fully offset" the benefit of $730 million in tariff refunds, Home Depot CFO Richard McPhail said last month.

"There's just so much uncertainty right now. … You think inflation, interest rates, fuel prices," McPhail said last week at a conference.

Among those hardest hit are manufacturers in the domestic automobile supply chain.

Lucerne International, a privately held auto parts maker based in suburban Detroit, stopped manufacturing operations in the U.S. and canceled plans last year for a $50 million aluminum forging plant in Michigan.

"The onset of the Trump tariffs 2.0 has just really torn holes in our global supply chains and increased costs significantly," Lucerne CEO Mary Buchzeiger said, citing higher costs for raw materials, including aluminum, as well as finished parts.

Buchzeiger, whose firm still manufactures overseas, said she has shifted U.S. operations to warehousing, distribution, and tariff-mitigation solutions for other companies, which offer "much better margins."

"There's no doubt that there's margin pressure for suppliers," Paul McCarthy, CEO of vehicle supplier trade association MEMA, said. "Some of it, we try to absorb … and then some of it does have to be passed on."

Growth, as measured by earnings before interest and taxes for the top 100 auto suppliers, fell last year to 4.2%, down from more than 6% in 2021, according to consulting firm Berylls by AlixPartners. Among the top 10 automakers, that figure is 5.2%, down from nearly 8% in 2022.

Not all auto companies have managed the additional costs. Spanish auto parts maker Grupo Antolin, which supplies components to automakers including Ford, GM, Volkswagen and Stellantis, filed for Chapter 15 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. in July. The company cited tariffs, higher raw-material and energy costs, and supply-chain disruptions as reasons for its restructuring.

Better off are the giants of the corporate world, like the tech and finance companies that fill the S&P 500. These firms typically have more cash reserves and take out long-term debt, insulating them somewhat from the sting of higher rates.

Most larger companies can thrive until borrowing costs rise much further. The pain would hit when the yield on the 10-year Treasury bond reaches 6%, up from around 5% now, according to JPMorgan's Lakos-Bujas, who cited 80 years of data.

Borrowing costs are expected to stay higher for longer. Persistent inflation, which forced Warsh to raise the benchmark Fed rate against Trump's wishes, along with heavy borrowing from the U.S. government, is keeping upward pressure on rates.

Across corporate America, companies are grappling with these shocks in different ways. The divide comes down to one question: Who has pricing power?

Some industries have learned they can readily pass higher costs on to consumers, while others are caught in a catch-22: If they raise prices too much, they risk destroying demand.

Airline executives last week boasted of higher fares as customers keep booking trips, especially abroad, allowing them to pass increased fuel costs on to travelers. Airlines scaled back growth plans, cutting less profitable flights even after the collapse of Spirit Airlines this year.

Fewer flights can mean pricier airline tickets, and fares were up more than 23% in August from last year, according to the latest inflation read. Yet even strong demand has its limits.

"The consumer has been incredibly, incredibly resilient," United Chief Financial Officer Mike Leskinen said Wednesday during a Morgan Stanley conference in Laguna Beach, California.

"But there's some marginal routes that don't make sense in a higher fuel environment. So we cut them," Leskinen said. "You should see us continue to ... behave that way."

Much of corporate America remains resilient despite higher fuel and financing costs. Profit margins for major companies hover near historic highs, propelled by strong productivity gains, labor costs that have stayed in check and surging artificial intelligence investment that is driving growth.

But a risk of Warsh's efforts is that higher rates don't directly address the root causes of inflation: the Iran war, the Trump administration's tariffs, and the AI boom, which has driven up the prices for everything required to build and run data centers, from electricity to memory chips, copper, and land.

Raising rates to tap the brakes on the U.S. economy could slow it down too much, or send stocks into a tailspin, said EY-Parthenon's Daco.

"The economy is resilient, but it's exposed to growing pockets of risk," he said. "A shock could materialize faster than we all think."

financeStories.fullTranslation:
航班减少且票价上涨。货运附加费层出不穷。制造商大举囤积库存。甚至走向破产。
对于规模各异的美国企业而言，唐纳德·特朗普总统贸易政策下征收的关税、伊朗战争引发的燃料价格飙升，以及如今不断上升的利率，三者叠加正迫使高管们做出艰难抉择。
艾伦·埃登（Allen Eden）一直在为其拥有25名员工的企业——位于爱荷华州布里特的Original Saw Co.——储备额外库存。该公司生产用于木工和金属加工的工业动力锯，目前他正在全力应对铝、钢材和关键零部件价格暴涨的局面。
举个例子：他说，今年夏天他所生产锯机电机上使用的一款“小支架”价格翻了一倍多，从42美元飙升至87美元。
“太糟糕了，”56岁的埃登告诉CNBC。“我只是尽量多备些货，因为我不知道以后还能不能买得到。”
对于横跨制造业、交通运输业和零售业的企业来说，这是一场来自三方的夹击：关税使原材料和商品变得更加昂贵；更高的燃料价格推高了生产和运输成本；而不断上升的利率又让企业维持运营所需的库存和设备融资成本变得更高。
尽管几乎没有哪个行业能完全免受这些压力的影响，但中型制造企业受到的挤压尤为严重。不断上涨的钢铁和燃料成本正迫使他们至少将部分开支通过提价转嫁出去，从而加剧了过去几年居高不下的顽固通胀。
然而，为了抑制通胀，美联储三年来首次上调利率，并暗示今年可能还会再次加息。这使得企业在面对更高的投入成本和用于卡车运输的柴油创纪录价格压缩利润空间的同时，为库存融资和借贷寻求扩张的成本也变得更加高昂。
埃登表示，其生产的锯机既向家得宝（Home Depot）等大型零售商销售，也直接供应给中小型制造商，这类产品的涨价似乎已不可避免。
这种痛苦并非均匀分布。摩根大通全球策略主管杜布拉夫科·拉科斯-布哈斯（Dubravko Lakos-Bujas）在9月14日的一份报告中表示，规模较小的企业通常依赖期限较短的贷款，这意味着美联储加息会更直接地转化为其成本负担。
但拉科斯-布哈斯指出，无论规模大小，制造业和设备供应商等资本密集型行业、包括卡车车队在内的物流公司以及商业地产，在利率上升的环境中也遭受了更大的打击。
安永旗下全球战略咨询机构安永-博智隆（EY-Parthenon）首席经济学家格雷戈里·达科（Gregory Daco）表示：“高利率与高燃料价格的结合意味着，在这两方面均有较大风险敞口的行业首当其冲。”
他表示：“任何类型的制造业都会不成比例地受到更高燃料价格的影响。”
不断上涨的燃料和大宗商品成本让原材料生产商及其服务的零售商都感受到了压力。
工业巨头伊士曼化工（Eastman Chemical）首席执行官马克·科斯塔（Mark Costa）在5月表示，利率和通胀的双重打击正将该行业逼入绝境。伊士曼生产的塑料、添加剂和其他材料广泛应用于医疗设备、动物饲料和汽车挡风玻璃等多种产品中。
“每个人都已被逼到了墙角，毫无消化这些涨幅的余地，”科斯塔说。“所有人都在极快地提价，速度之快是我20年来从未见过的。”
在零售方面，家得宝首席财务官理查德·麦克菲尔（Richard McPhail）上个月表示，来自能源和原材料成本的意外压力将“完全抵消”7.3亿美元关税退税带来的收益。
“眼下充斥着太多不确定性。……你会想到通胀、利率、燃料价格，”麦克菲尔上周在一次会议上表示。
受打击最严重的群体中包括国内汽车供应链上的制造商。
总部位于底特律郊区的私营汽车零部件制造商卢塞恩国际（Lucerne International）停止了在美的制造业务，并在去年取消了在密歇根州投资5000万美元建设铝锻造厂的计划。
“特朗普关税2.0的启动确实撕裂了我们的全球供应链，并大幅推高了成本，”卢塞恩首席执行官玛丽·布赫齐格（Mary Buchzeiger）表示，她提到了包括铝在内的原材料以及成品零部件成本的上升。
布赫齐格的公司仍在海外进行制造，她表示已将美国本土业务转向仓储、分销以及为其他公司提供规避关税影响的解决方案，这些业务带来了“好得多的利润率”。
“毫无疑问，供应商面临着利润率压力，”汽车供应商行业协会MEMA首席执行官保罗·麦卡锡（Paul McCarthy）表示。“其中一部分，我们尽量自行消化……然后另一部分则不得不转嫁出去。”
根据咨询公司AlixPartners旗下Berylls的数据，以息税前利润衡量，排名前100位的汽车供应商去年的增长率降至4.2%，低于2021年的6%以上。在排名前10位的汽车制造商中，这一数字为5.2%，低于2022年的近8%。
并非所有汽车公司都能承受这些额外成本。为福特、通用、大众和Stellantis等汽车制造商供应零部件的西班牙汽车零部件制造商安东林集团（Grupo Antolin）于7月在美国申请了破产法第15章破产保护。该企业将关税、更高的原材料及能源成本以及供应链中断列为重组的原因。
日子较好过的是企业界的巨头，比如占据标普500指数权重的科技和金融公司。这些企业通常拥有更多现金储备，并借入长期债务，从而在一定程度上抵御了加息带来的刺痛。
大多数大型企业在借贷成本进一步大幅攀升之前仍能维持良好运转。摩根大通的拉科斯-布哈斯引用80年的数据指出，当10年期美国国债收益率从目前的5%左右攀升至6%时，痛苦才会真正来临。
预计借贷成本将在更长时间内保持在较高水平。顽固的通胀迫使沃什（Warsh）顶住特朗普的意愿提高了美联储基准利率，加之美国政府的大额借贷，持续对利率施加上行压力。
在整个美国企业界，各家公司正以不同方式应对这些冲击。分歧最终归结为一个问题：谁拥有定价权？
一些行业已经发现他们可以轻易将更高的成本转嫁给消费者，而另一些行业则陷入了两难困境：如果提价过多，就有破坏需求的风险。
航空公司高管上周夸耀称机票价格有所上涨，因为乘客仍在持续预订出行，尤其是出国旅行，这使他们能够将增加的燃料成本转嫁给旅客。即使在今年精神航空（Spirit Airlines）倒闭之后，航空公司也缩减了扩张计划，削减了利润较低的航班。
航班减少可能意味着机票更加昂贵，根据最新的通胀数据，8月份机票价格同比上涨超过23%。然而，即便是强劲的需求也是有极限的。

“消费者的韧性极其、极其出色，”联合航空首席财务官迈克·莱斯金宁（Mike Leskinen）周三在加利福尼亚州拉古纳海滩举行的摩根士丹利会议上表示。
“但是在燃料成本较高的环境下，一些边缘航线就不再具备合理性了。因此我们砍掉了这些航线，”莱斯金宁说，“大家应该会看到我们继续……采取这种做法。”
尽管燃料和融资成本上升，美国大部分企业依然保持着韧性。在强劲的生产率增长、得到控制的劳动力成本以及推动增长的激增人工智能投资的推动下，主要企业的利润率徘徊在历史高位附近。
但沃什（Warsh）相关举措的一个风险在于，更高的利率并不能直接解决通货膨胀的根本原因：伊朗战争、特朗普政府的关税，以及人工智能热潮——后者推高了建设和运营数据中心所需一切物品的价格，从电力到存储芯片、铜以及土地。
安永帕特农（EY-Parthenon）的达科（Daco）表示，通过加息来给美国经济踩刹车可能会使其放缓过度，或者导致股市陷入暴跌。
“经济具有韧性，但正面临越来越多的潜在风险，”他说，“冲击显现的速度可能比我们所有人想象的都要快。”

financeStories.title: 乳晕纹身师对网络审查感到“沮丧”
financeStories.fullContent:
A medical tattoo artist has described the online censorship of nipple tattoos for mastectomy patients as "wholly unfair and discriminatory".

Lauren Carter, based in Hanham near Bristol, says social media bots and algorithms often mistakenly flag her hyper-realistic work as "inappropriate nudity".

Carter has been banned from posting numerous times, and her pictures have been permanently removed, which she says leaves her "struggling" to reach new clients.

A spokesperson for Facebook and Instagram owner Meta said it "continues to work on improving" how it identifies and protects medical and health-related content.

Because medical tattoos are designed to look as realistic as possible, social media bots and algorithms can sometimes confuse the inked 3D-effect for bare skin.

A Meta spokesperson confirmed post-mastectomy scarring and areola tattoos are allowed on Facebook and Instagram, but its systems "occasionally make mistakes".

"We understand how frustrating that can be, which is why we allow users to appeal these decisions and we continue to work on improving how we identify and protect medical and health-related content," they said.

"We recognise the important role medical tattooists play in supporting breast cancer survivors, and we want this content on our platforms."

Despite posting disclaimers and covering the nipple tattoo with emojis, Carter says each update to her online portfolio jeopardises years of hard work and positive reviews.

"It really does upset me - there's a sense of injustice," she said.

"I'm annoyed and frustrated, not only for myself, but for the people who are looking for this sort of thing and can't find it. I don't know how else to reach people."

Carter says her posts are automatically removed "nine times out of 10". She always appeals the decision, but "it's as if nobody even reads it".

"It's interesting how the photos I post of male nipples following my treatments do not get banned or reported as a sexual image," she added.

"For me, this work is about so much more than beauty. It is about helping people feel confident, comfortable and like themselves again."

Jessica Bowler, a nurse from Bristol, underwent a double mastectomy with implant reconstruction at the age of 32 following a breast cancer diagnosis in 2019.

"Although I knew the treatment was necessary to save my life, it was still incredibly difficult physically and emotionally," she said.

"I would look in the mirror and almost not recognise myself. My chest was a reminder of everything I had been through."

Bowler said the decision to get areola reconstruction tattoos marked an important milestone in her recovery, describing the procedure as "empowering".

"The tattoos weren't about vanity; they were about feeling comfortable in my own skin," she said.

"It's difficult to explain unless you've been through it, but having something restored that cancer took away can be incredibly powerful."

The 39-year-old described the online censoring of nipple tattoos as "really upsetting", as it prevents survivors from exploring the options available to them post-surgery.

"They shouldn't be treated as something shameful or sexual," she said.

"[People] who've been through breast cancer should be able to share their stories and help each other without being censored."

financeStories.fullTranslation:
一名医疗纹身师将针对乳房切除术患者乳头纹身的网络审查描述为“完全不公且具有歧视性”。

来自布里斯托附近汉汉姆（Hanham）的劳伦·卡特（Lauren Carter）表示，社交媒体的机器人和算法经常错误地将她极度逼真的作品标记为“不当裸露”。

卡特曾多次被禁止发帖，她的照片也被永久删除，她说这导致她“难以”接触到新客户。

Facebook和Instagram的母公司Meta的发言人表示，该公司“正在继续改进”识别和保护医疗健康相关内容的方式。

由于医疗纹身旨在尽可能逼真，社交媒体机器人和算法有时会混淆纹出的3D效果与真实的裸露皮肤。

Meta发言人证实，Facebook和Instagram允许发布乳房切除术后疤痕和乳晕纹身，但其系统“偶尔会犯错”。

他们表示：“我们理解这有多么令人沮丧，这就是为什么我们允许用户对这些决定提出申诉，并且我们正在继续努力改进识别和保护医疗健康相关内容的方式。”

“我们认识到医疗纹身师在支持乳腺癌康复者方面所发挥的重要作用，我们希望这些内容出现在我们的平台上。”

尽管发布了免责声明并用表情符号遮盖了乳头纹身，卡特表示，她在网络作品集上的每一次更新都会危及多年来的辛勤工作和好评。

“这真的很让我难过——有一种不公感，”她说。

“我感到恼火和沮丧，不仅是为我自己，也是为了那些正在寻找这类服务却找不到的人。我不知道还能通过什么途径接触到需要的人。”

卡特说，她的帖子“十有八九”会被自动删除。她每次都会对决定提出申诉，但“就像根本没人看一样”。

“有趣的是，在治疗后我发布的男性乳头照片，并没有被封禁或被举报为色情图像，”她补充道。

“对我来说，这项工作远不止关于美丽。它是关于帮助人们重新感到自信、舒适，找回属于自己的感觉。”

来自布里斯托的护士杰西卡·鲍勒（Jessica Bowler）在2019年被诊断出患有乳腺癌后，于32岁时接受了双侧乳房切除术及假体再造术。

“虽然我知道这种治疗对挽救我的生命是必要的，但在身体和情感上仍然极其艰难，”她说。

“我看着镜子，几乎认不出自己。我的胸部提醒着我所经历的一切。”

鲍勒表示，决定进行乳晕再造纹身是她康复过程中的一个重要里程碑，她形容这一过程是“赋予力量的”。

“这些纹身与虚荣无关；它们关乎让自己在身体里感到舒适，”她说。

“除非你亲身经历过，否则很难解释，但能把癌症夺走的东西恢复过来，会具有极其强大的力量。”

这位39岁的女士将网络上对乳头纹身的审查描述为“非常令人心烦”，因为这阻碍了康复者探索术后可供他们选择的方案。

“它们不应该被当作可耻或色情的事物来看待，”她说。

“经历过乳腺癌的人应该能够分享他们的故事并互相帮助，而不应受到审查。”

来自肯特郡海斯（Hythe）的玛雅（Maya）今年13岁，她在三岁时被诊断出患有神经母细胞瘤。

苏珊·加森（Susan Gasson）自20世纪80年代以来经历过四次癌症，目前正在参加一项试验，每天服用一片药物。

从“无尽滚动”到战胜孤独，专家和用户讨论婴儿潮一代如何使用社交媒体。

31岁的格蕾丝·沃登（Grace Warden）表示，她“没有预料到”自己将要面对的副作用的严重程度。

在短信交流和谈话中，多位曾就职于领先公司的人士对这些警告表示怀疑。

financeStories.fullContent:
Your window to save up to $200 is closing fast. Current ticket pricing ends Sept. 25 at 11:59 p.m. PT. After that, prices go up.

At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, getting ahead means more than sitting in on great sessions. It means meeting the people you need to know, seeing what’s coming before it hits the mainstream, and getting practical insights you can put to work.

TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 brings 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders together for three days of ideas, connections, and opportunities across the startup ecosystem.

With 250+ speakers covering 200+ sessions across six industry stages, roundtables, and breakouts, you’ll get practical insight into the forces changing how companies are built, funded, and scaled, from AI and robotics to fintech, infrastructure, and the future of work. But the value isn’t just onstage.

Make the connections. Meet potential investors, clients, partners, hires, and collaborators through networking, including AI-powered matchmaking, ad hoc meetings, and the Deal Flow Cafe if you’re an investor or founder.

Stay ahead of the market. Hear how leaders are approaching the biggest strategic questions around AI, competitive advantage, fundraising, talent, go-to-market, and scaling.

See what’s next before it becomes obvious. Explore 300+ startups and breakthroughs in the Expo Hall, watch the intense pitch competition called Startup Battlefield 200, and discover emerging technologies across all sessions.

Leave with something you can use. From fundraising strategies to GTM tactics and insights on building defensible companies in the AI era, Disrupt is built around actionable ideas, not just big conversations.

The people you need to meet, the ideas you need to hear, and the opportunities you don’t want to miss will all be in San Francisco this October.

Join 10,000+ founders, VCs, and tech operators on October 13–15 at San Francisco. Get your ticket by Sept. 25 at 11:59 p.m. PT and save up to $200 before prices rise. Save an additional 30% on group passes of four or more.

financeStories.title: 确定性核心，非确定性外壳
financeStories.fullContent:
Fourteen years ago, Gary Bernhardt coined the term Functional Core, Imperative Shell . Like most good ideas in computing it was not entirely new, but his conception had great clarity, and it forms an excellent basis for talking about testing and determinism in existing systems.

Briefly, Functional Core/Imperative Shell architecture divides the code into two parts. The Functional Core is purely functional - that is no IO, and no destructive state updates. It is concerned with the business logic of the application. The Imperative Shell has comparatively little pathing, but maintains state, coordinates external dependencies, and deals with the outside world - that is to say IO. Its job is to query the core with values, receive values back as the result of some blackbox decision, and use that to interact with the outside world; whether that's writing to a database, sending a request, or updating a GUI.

The Shell and the Core in this model have distinct characteristics:

This makes the core very amenable to testing. Since it's purely functional, the same inputs will always get the same results. Since it's isolated, there is nothing to mock or stub. And since it handles complex business logic, the tests can tell us a lot about how the system behaves.

A shorter way of describing the properties that make pure functions amenable to testing is that they are deterministic. That is - given a stream of inputs, a pure function always returns the same stream of outputs; their behaviour is repeatable. But pure functional programming is not the only way to get there. If we tilt our heads a little we can see that a stream of values and a sequence of assignments are different ways of expressing the same thing, and State Machines can bring us the same benefits. Consider the following code:

The function add is easy to reason about; it's pure and thus deterministic. But the AddMachine is also deterministic - given the same sequence of calls to the transition function, AddMachine will return the same state. It being imperative does not change that.

Pure functional programming is a fine paradigm, but due to language or performance considerations, it is not always practical - I would not want to try it in C! But weakening the requirements from purely functional to merely deterministic, we retain the testability benefits of "Functional Core, Imperative Shell", while broadening its applicability. And so the title of this post: Deterministic Core, Non-Deterministic Shell.

Determinism can feel like a more abstract concept than functional purity. How do you know it when you see it? I find it's easier to start with what is not deterministic and work backwards. Here are some common examples of non-repeatable behaviour:

All these belong in the non-deterministic shell. Whenever you find them in your business logic, you have a natural target for defragmentation - either splitting the function in two around them, or lifting them up a layer and injecting their result as a parameter. It's illustrative to think of the "shell" metaphor quite literally; it should surround the logic, querying the heart of the application to get what it needs.

"This is all well and good", you might think, "but what use of it is to me, toiling away in the legacy & vibe-code mines of industry?". A fair accusation, imaginary reader; not everyone can be Foundation DB and make that distinction from day one (they actually went a step further, but that's a topic for another post). Determinism and non-determinism are highly entwined in almost every real life codebase I have seen, and I've seen my fair share.

But don't let perfect be the enemy of good! One way to think of your average (ie, terrible) codebase is that it has many deterministic cores. There are thousands, strewn through the slop as stars in the sky. The glass half empty take is these codebases are an irredeemable legacy mess. But glass half full is that there are many deterministic cores hidden somewhere inside, and maybe only a handful.

Users of older Windows systems may remember the "Disk Defragmenter"; it took files whose contents were scattered physically across the spinning hard disk and made them contiguous. In an era where read speed depended on physical distance on the media, this mattered a lot.

So one gradual approach for existing code is to practice the Defragmentation of Determinism. Identify it wherever you can - files, classes, even a few lines in individual functions - and start collecting them. The more determinism that can be grouped, the more easily testable functionality you have, and the more you can feel confident about the behaviour and reliability of the program as a whole. The surface area for "hard to test" (non-deterministic code) starts to shrink. On a large enough codebase you will likely never get to a single deterministic core, but even hundreds is better than thousands.

Every nasty mess of a codebase I've seen has one or more much nicer deterministic state machines locked inside. I promise you they are there, even if it's not obvious. And once you find them, you'll be delighted with how much easier the software is to modify and test. Piece by piece, reliability can be wrought.
financeStories.fullTranslation:
十四年前，加里·伯恩哈特（Gary Bernhardt）提出了“函数式核心，命令式外壳”（Functional Core, Imperative Shell）这一概念。就像计算机领域大多数优秀思想一样，它并非全新之物，但他的构想极其清晰，为探讨现有系统中的测试与确定性打下了绝佳的基础。

简而言之，“函数式核心/命令式外壳”架构将代码分为两部分。函数式核心是纯函数的——也就是说没有输入输出（I/O），也没有破坏性的状态更新。它专注于应用程序的业务逻辑。命令式外壳包含的分支路径相对较少，但负责维护状态、协调外部依赖并与外部世界交互——也就是进行 I/O。它的职责是以输入值调用核心，接收黑盒决策结果所返回的值，并利用这些值与外部世界互动；无论是写入数据库、发送网络请求，还是更新图形用户界面（GUI）。

在这种模型中，外壳和核心具有截然不同的特征：

这使得核心非常易于测试。由于它是纯函数的，相同的输入将始终获得相同的结果。由于它是隔离的，不需要进行任何模拟（mock）或存根（stub）。而且由于它处理的是复杂的业务逻辑，测试能够让我们深入了解系统的具体行为。

用一种更简短的方式来描述让纯函数易于测试的特性，那就是它们具有“确定性”（deterministic）。也就是说——给定一系列输入流，纯函数始终返回相同的输出流；它们的行为是可重复的。但纯函数式编程并不是实现这一目标的唯一途径。如果我们换个角度思考，就会发现值流与一系列赋值语句不过是同一事物的不同表达方式，而状态机同样可以为我们带来相同的好处。试看以下代码：

函数 add 很容易推导理解；它是纯函数，因此具有确定性。但 AddMachine 同样具有确定性——给定对状态转移函数的相同调用序列，AddMachine 将返回相同的状态。它是命令式的这一事实并不会改变这一点。

纯函数式编程是一种优秀的范式，但出于语言或性能方面的考虑，它并不总是切实可行的——我可不想在 C 语言里尝试它！但如果我们将要求从“纯函数式”放宽至仅仅具备“确定性”，我们就能在保留“函数式核心，命令式外壳”可测试性优势的同时，拓宽其适用范围。因此便有了本文的标题：确定性核心，非确定性外壳。

相比函数纯度，确定性可能感觉是一个更抽象的概念。你如何一眼识别出它？我发现从“什么不是确定性的”入手反向推导会更容易。以下是非重复行为的一些常见例子：

所有这些都属于非确定性外壳。只要你在业务逻辑中发现了它们，你就找到了进行整理重构的绝佳切入点——要么围绕它们将函数拆分为两部分，要么将它们提升一层并将它们的结果作为参数注入。形象地将“外壳”这个隐喻从字面意义上去理解会很有启发；它应当包裹在业务逻辑周围，通过向应用程序的核心发起调用来获取所需内容。

你可能会想：“这一切听起来都很棒，但对于像我这样在工业界遗留代码和凭借直觉乱堆的代码堆里苦苦挣扎的人来说，这有什么用呢？”虚构的读者朋友，这是一个合情合理的质问；并不是每个人都能成为 FoundationDB，并从第一天起就划清这种界限（他们实际上走得更远，不过那是另一篇文章的主题了）。在我见过的几乎每一个现实代码库中，确定性与非确定性都高度交织在一起，而我见过的代码库可不算少。

但不要让完美成为优秀的敌人！理解你手头普通（即糟糕）代码库的一种方式是，把它看作拥有许多确定性核心。成千上万个核心散落在这堆乱码中，犹如夜空中的繁星。悲观的角度看，这些代码库是不可救药的遗留烂摊子；但乐观的角度看，里面隐藏着许多确定性核心，也许整理出来只有少数几个模块。

老一代 Windows 系统的用户可能还记得“磁盘碎片整理程序”；它把物理上散布在旋转硬盘各处的文件内容重新排布为连续空间。在那个读取速度取决于介质上物理距离的时代，这一点至关重要。

因此，处理现有代码的一种渐进式方法就是实践“确定性的碎片整理”。尽可能去识别确定性——文件、类、甚至是单个函数中的几行代码——并开始将它们收集归拢。能够聚集的确定性越多，你拥有的易于测试的功能就越多，你就对整个程序的行为和可靠性更有信心。“难以测试”（即非确定性代码）的暴露面开始缩小。在足够庞大的代码库中，你可能永远无法归结为一个单一的确定性核心，但哪怕整理成几百个，也远比散落成千上万处要好。

我见过的每一个乱作一团的代码库里，都深锁着一个或多个极其优雅的确定性状态机。我向你保证它们确实存在，哪怕并不显眼。一旦你找到了它们，你会惊叹于软件的修改和测试变得如此轻松。一点一滴，可靠性自能筑就。
keyTakeaways: Gary Bernhardt在14年前提出了术语“Functional Core, Imperative Shell（函数式核心，命令式外壳）”。
Functional Core/Imperative Shell 架构将代码划分为无I/O、无破坏性状态更新的纯函数式核心，以及负责协调外部依赖和处理I/O的命令式外壳两部分。
来源叙事重点：主张将 Gary Bernhardt 的“函数式核心/命令式外壳”泛化为“确定性核心/非确定性外壳”，强调通过确定性状态机降低纯函数门槛，并倡导采用“确定性碎片整理”策略对工业界遗留代码进行渐进式重构。

evidence.quote: Fourteen years ago, Gary Bernhardt coined the term Functional Core, Imperative Shell .

Briefly, Functional Core/Imperative Shell architecture divides the code into two parts. The Functional Core is purely functional - that is no IO, and no destructive state updates. It is concerned with the business logic of the application. The Imperative Shell has comparatively little pathing, but maintains state, coordinates external dependencies, and deals with the outside world - that is to say IO.
not everyone can be Foundation DB and make that distinction from day one (they actually went a step further, but that's a topic for another post).
Users of older Windows systems may remember the "Disk Defragmenter"; it took files whose contents were scattered physically across the spinning hard disk and made them contiguous.

position.sourceRole: 技术博主与软件工程实践经验分享者，面向技术社区提供实战型架构与重构思考。
position.narrativeFocus: 主张将 Gary Bernhardt 的“函数式核心/命令式外壳”泛化为“确定性核心/非确定性外壳”，强调通过确定性状态机降低纯函数门槛，并倡导采用“确定性碎片整理”策略对工业界遗留代码进行渐进式重构。
stakeholders: 一线软件开发工程师
系统架构师
遗留系统维护团队
测试与质量保障（QA）工程师
函数式编程倡导者
consensus: 将核心业务逻辑与 I/O 等副作用隔离能显著提高代码的可测试性与可靠性。
纯函数与确定性逻辑由于具备可重复性（相同输入得到相同输出/状态），无需复杂 Mock 即可快速验证。
工业界现实代码库普遍存在确定性与非确定性行为深度交织混杂的现状。
disagreements: 核心架构是否必须严格坚持无状态更新的“纯函数式”，还是可以妥协放宽至包含命令式状态更新但行为可重复的“确定性状态机”。
面对极端复杂的遗留混乱代码，投入工程成本进行渐进式“碎片整理”重构是否比保持现状或整套重写更划算。
blindSpots: 未深入探讨在高度并发或分布式场景下，确定性状态机在应对时序竞争、网络分区时的状态协调成本。
缺乏对非确定性边界（如时间依赖、随机数、外部硬件交互）在依赖注入时带来的接口膨胀与性能开销的具体评估。
过于乐观预设开发者能够清晰辨识并低风险剥离交织在业务逻辑深处的隐式副作用。

financeStories.fullContent:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast

Dan Tehan , the shadow minister for energy, said Gallagher’s criticism of the Coalition’s fuel plan wasn’t fair.

Tehan said the call for a 50% cut to the fuel excise whenever barrels of oil top US$100 was a “good, sensible, practical measure” that would help Australians deal with a cost of living crisis. He told RN:

[What] I would say to Anthony Albanese and the Labor party is get out amongst the people and see what’s happening in your electorates because people are hurting because of cost of living …

We have the discipline to be able to do the policy work to make sure we can offset policies like this so it won’t be inflationary and it will provide much needed relief to people, and they need it now.

Obviously we’ve helped when the war started with some changes to the fuel excise but we’ve shifted, and [are] including in the budget, to providing more permanent cost of living arrangements, including through the tax system, to make sure that that ongoing cost-of-living help is there permanently, not just in these one-off arrangements, which, when we’ve got higher inflation, could be difficult in the economy.

Our decisions have been built and baked into the budget to make sure that that cost-of-living help is permanent. You know, the sooner this war in the Middle East stops, the better.

影子能源部长丹·特汉（Dan Tehan）表示，加拉格尔（Gallagher）对联盟党燃油方案的批评是不公平的。

特汉表示，呼吁在每桶石油价格超过100美元时将燃油税削减50%，是一项“良好、明智、切实可行的举措”，将帮助澳大利亚人应对生活成本危机。他对RN（澳大利亚广播公司国家广播电台）表示：

“我想对安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯和工党说的是，走到民众中去，看看你们的选区正在发生什么，因为人们正饱受生活成本之苦……

我们有能力且有纪律推进政策制定工作，以确保我们能够冲抵此类政策的影响，使其不至于推高通胀，并为民众提供急需的救济，而且他们现在就需要这种救济。

显然，战争爆发时我们曾通过调整燃油消费税提供过帮助，但我们已经做出了调整，并正在纳入预算之中，以提供更具长期性的生活成本支持方案（包括通过税收系统），确保这种持续的生活成本援助是长久存在的，而不仅仅是这些在通胀高企时可能会给经济带来困难的一次性举措。

我们的决定已经制定并融入到预算案中，以确保生活成本援助具有长期性。要知道，中东的这场战争越早结束越好。”

financeStories.title: 喷气机末节崩盘遭包装工逆转，加时告负错失2015年以来首次2胜0负开局
financeStories.originalTitle: Jets collapse late against Packers, miss chance at first 2-0 start since 2015 in overtime loss
financeStories.snippet: The New York Jets blew a 17-7 fourth quarter lead as the Green Bay Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime at MetLife Stadium.
financeStories.fullContent:
For most of Sunday afternoon, the New York Jets looked poised to move to 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Jets controlled most of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, but made some crucial errors down the stretch to cough up their 10-point fourth-quarter lead.

The Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime, with Trey Smack kicking a 26-yard field goal to complete the comeback.

Green Bay struck first on a 6-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to MarShawn Lloyd in the second quarter, but the Jets answered with a 5-yard touchdown run from Braelon Allen. Geno Smith connected with Garrett Wilson for a 5-yard score in the third quarter to give New York a 14-7 lead.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Jets appeared to have delivered the knockout blow early in the fourth quarter when they recovered a Lloyd fumble at the Green Bay 18-yard line. But the offense couldn't move the ball and settled for a 32-yard Jason Sanders field goal, extending the lead to 17-7 with 11:04 remaining.

That's when everything started to unravel.

A 38-yard pass-interference penalty helped Green Bay march down the field before Love found Christian Watson for a 3-yard touchdown. The Jets failed to pick up a first down on their next possession, and Skyy Moore returned the ensuing punt 63 yards to the New York 19-yard line. Smack kicked a 34-yard field goal four plays later to tie the game.

New York still had a chance to win in regulation. After Breece Hall gained just one yard on third-and-2, the Jets faced fourth-and-1 at midfield with 1:20 remaining. Aaron Glenn kept his offense on the field rather than punting, an aggressive decision to try to win the game. It's hard to fault Glenn for trusting his offense to gain one yard, but Braelon Allen was stuffed. Green Bay failed to capitalize, sending the game to overtime.

The Jets received the ball first in overtime and the possession was a complete disaster. The Packers sacked Smith on consecutive plays, the offense committed a false-start penalty and New York faced a third-and-30 from their own 10-yard line before eventually punting on fourth down.

Green Bay then moved 58 yards on four offensive plays, aided by an unnecessary roughness penalty against Jarvis Brownlee Jr., before Smack ended the game on the fifth play of the drive.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Penalties were a problem for both teams throughout the game. Green Bay was flagged 14 times for 133 yards, while New York committed 13 penalties for 156 yards. That's an absurd 27 accepted penalties for 289 yards.

But the timing of the Jets' two biggest penalties proved especially costly: the 38-yard pass-interference call aided Green Bay's fourth-quarter touchdown drive, while Brownlee's 15-yard penalty moved the Packers into position for the winning field goal.

Smith completed 27-of-41 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. It wasn't a spectacular performance, but it should have been good enough given how well New York's defense played.

That's what makes the loss particularly brutal for the Jets. New York outgained Green Bay 285-199, held the Packers to 1-of-9 on third down, won the turnover battle and possessed the ball for nearly 11 minutes longer. Love threw for just 145 yards, although he threw two touchdowns and avoided turning the ball over.

The Jets had the game won and a chance to send the MetLife Stadium crowd home believing in a 2-0 team . Instead, they gave the game away and sent their fans home wondering how they managed to blow another one.

在周日下午的大部分时间里，纽约喷气机队看起来都胜券在握，有望迎来2015年以来的首次2胜0负开局。在大都会人寿体育场对阵绿湾包装工队的比赛中，喷气机队掌控了大部分时间的局势，但在最后关头犯下了几次致命错误，白白葬送了第四节10分的领先优势。

包装工队连得13分，在加时赛中以20-17获胜，特雷·斯马克（Trey Smack）命中一记26码的射门，完成了这场逆转。

绿湾队在第二节率先发难，乔丹·洛夫（Jordan Love）助攻马肖恩·劳埃德（MarShawn Lloyd）完成6码达阵传球，但喷气机队随后凭借布雷隆·艾伦（Braelon Allen）的5码达阵冲跑还以颜色。第三节，吉诺·史密斯（Geno Smith）与加勒特·威尔逊（Garrett Wilson）连线完成5码达阵得分，让纽约队以14-7取得领先。

点击此处获取更多OUTKICK体育报道

第四节初，喷气机队在绿湾队18码线上抢回了劳埃德的掉球，看似已经给予对手致命一击。但随后进攻端停滞不前，只能由杰森·桑德斯（Jason Sanders）命中一记32码射门，在比赛还剩11分04秒时将领先优势扩大到17-7。

正是从那一刻起，局势开始全面崩盘。

一次38码的传球干扰犯规帮助绿湾队大步推进，随后洛夫连线克里斯蒂安·沃森（Christian Watson）完成3码达阵。喷气机队在接下来的进攻轮次中未能取得首攻，天魔·摩尔（Skyy Moore）将随后的弃踢回攻63码，推进至纽约队19码线。四档进攻后，斯马克命中一记34码射门，将比分扳平。

纽约队在常规时间仍有获胜机会。在布里斯·霍尔（Breece Hall）于三档2码仅推进1码后，喷气机队在比赛还剩1分20秒时面临中场附近的四档1码。主教练阿隆·格伦（Aaron Glenn）没有选择弃踢，而是让进攻组留在场上，做出了一个试图直接拿下比赛的激进决定。很难指责格伦信任自己的进攻组去争取这短短1码，但布雷隆·艾伦的冲球被防守组死死阻截。绿湾队随后未能在常规时间转化为得分，比赛进入加时赛。

喷气机队在加时赛中率先获得球权，但这次进攻堪称一场彻底的灾难。包装工队连续两次抄截史密斯，进攻组又出现一次提前移动犯规，导致纽约队在本方10码线面临三档30码的绝境，最终只能在四档弃踢。

随后，在贾维斯·布朗利二世（Jarvis Brownlee Jr.）被判非必要粗暴犯规的帮助下，绿湾队仅用四次进攻就推进了58码，接着斯马克在这次进攻序列的第五档完成终结绝杀。

克雷格·卡顿秀——直率、犀利、不容错过。立即下载他的每日播客！

犯规整场比赛都困扰着双方。绿湾队被罚14次、罚退133码，而纽约队则出现13次犯规、罚退156码。两队被判罚并接受的犯规累计达到了惊人的27次，总计罚退289码。

然而，喷气机队两次代价最为惨重的犯规发生时机极其致命：那次38码的传球干扰犯规直接助推了绿湾队第四节的达阵推进，而布朗利的15码粗暴犯规更是直接将包装工队送入了绝杀射门的有效射程。

史密斯全场41投27中，推进247码，收获1次达阵，无抄截。这算不上极其惊艳的发挥，但考虑到纽约队防守组的出色表现，这样的数据本应足以赢下比赛。

这正是这场失利让喷气机队尤为痛心疾首的原因所在。纽约队在总推进码数上以285-199领先绿湾队，将包装工队的三档转换限制为9投仅1中，在失误比上占优，且控球时间足足多了近11分钟。洛夫全场仅传出145码，不过他送出了两次达阵并且没有失误送球。

喷气机队本已胜券在握，本有机会让大都会人寿体育场的球迷坚信这是一支能取得2胜0负的队伍并满意而归。然而，他们亲手将胜利拱手相让，让球迷在退场时只能再次陷入沉思：他们究竟是怎么又搞砸了一场比赛？
